studies.title: Costa Chica · Alingo accompaniment study
studies.region: Costa Chica reference; a named chamber arrangement, not Mixteca yaa sii
studies.evidence: Published notation supplies the two-bar piano-secondo chord and bass onsets in Alingo Lingo, arranged by María Carpio and documented by Diana Laura Galeana Leyva, UNAM 2025, Figure 8, bars 102–103. One-reader rhythmic reduction; local musician review pending.
studies.note: The chord cue keeps quarter/eighth/eighth/quarter in each 6/8 bar; the bass crosses three quarter notes in bar one and dotted-quarter/eighth/quarter in bar two. These simultaneous layers do not change the meter or the dotted-quarter count. Compás authors all pitches, drum support, levels, 96 dotted-quarter BPM, fills and live form. The pluck is a single percussive cue, not the source piano chords, harp or guitar. No melody, complete source song or recording is embedded.

studies.title: Bembé · Pusztai bell/block study

studies.evidence: Published notation by Csabi Pusztai: Bembe Version 1.0, bar 1, supplies the bell and dotted-quarter block; Version 2.0, bar 1, supplies the first-and-second-eighth block variation. One-reader notation reduction; musician review pending.
studies.note: Two 12/8 bars, 48 sixteenths and eight dotted-quarter pulses. Base retains the lesson-one bell and block. Lift adds the second eighth of each pulse from lesson two. Compás authors 96 dotted-quarter BPM, levels, timbres, fills and conductor form. The spare lanes are silent: no bass, conga ensemble, sacred function, full lesson or source recording is claimed.
